Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <1143240089.8...@e56g2000cwe.googlegroups.com>,

echia...@yahoo.com writes:
>Wasn't there actually a ruling a while back that said "Prevent up to X"
>was supposed to be treated at "Prevent X"?

Effects that prevent "up to X" damage and effects that "prevent X"
damage mean the same thing. In both cases, applying the effect prevents
X damage. If fewer than X points of (preventable) damage are being
resolved, then the effect prevents all of those points.

--

The key words in this is "and prevent up to 1 damage" Preventing zero
damage is below 1 and therefore perfectly acceptable in this instance.
The card text provides an option, not a "must do" effect. You could
(theoreticly) play "prevent damage from this strike", wait till your
opponent drops a blur and then use the prevent provided from U.P. in
their 2nd (theoretical) "one agg" strike as it is still "later this
round"

Messages.Author: jeff...@pacbell.net
Messages.Body:


It sounds to me like the "later in this round" is the key phrase. This
allows you to play the card for a maneuver and gives you the option to
use the other effect at any time later. Other cards with the "prevent
up to" phrase don't say this so they must be used immediately when
damage prevention is applicable. Otherwise any "up to" card could be
used on a Theft of Vitae or any other non-damaging strike during the
damage prevention portion of combat.

Jeff

>"later this round" Nor does it prevent you from playing it to prevent

This last sentence doesn't make sense.

At inferior, there has to be damage to prevent or you can't play it. At
superior, it's played during choose range. There's no "zero damage"
floating round for you to prevent, and by the time you take damage this
round the card has already been played.
